title: Causes for IT Glitch that Resulted in Patients Receiving Mislabelled Medicines
what_it_is: Causes for IT Glitch that Resulted in Patients Receiving Mislabelled Medicines

sections.label: GP Connect medication label errors
sections.summary: A GP Connect system upgrade caused some clinics to print wrong units of measurement on medication labels, which IHiS investigated and addressed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Following a system upgrade by an information technology (IT) vendor for general practitioner (GP) Connect implemented on 1 September, some GP clinics encountered problems where some medication labels were printed wrongly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: While the correct medication and the total quantity of medication were correctly dispensed, the system printed the wrong Unit of Measurement (UOM) on the label.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Once notified, Integrated Health Information System (IHiS), the public healthcare IT agency and owner of the GP Connect system, investigated the incident, informed all affected clinics from 2 September, and provided support to the clinics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: No further errors have been reported since 3 September.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Affected patients were monitored by the clinics and, to date, there have not been any reports of adverse effects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Investigations revealed that the IT vendor had made some changes to the application code which resulted in incorrect medication labels being printed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Hence, the user acceptance tests designed to evaluate the upgrade did not pick up the error.

sections.label: Fault lies with IT vendor
sections.summary: The fault lies with the IT vendor, which changed the application code without informing IHiS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As the error was executed as a result of the IT vendor changing the application code without informing IHiS, the fault actually lies with the IT vendor.
